reserve

Extends the capacity of the archetype by factor 2 using power-of-2 allocation strategy.

def reserve(mut self)

Doubles the current capacity (minimum 8) to provide exponential growth that minimizes the frequency of memory reallocations while maintaining reasonable memory usage. This follows standard container growth patterns optimized for amortized performance.

Args:

  • self (Self)

Extends the capacity of the archetype to at least the specified number of entities.

def reserve(mut self, new_capacity: Int)

Uses a power-of-2 allocation strategy to ensure optimal memory alignment and reduce fragmentation. The actual allocated capacity will be the next power of 2 greater than or equal to the requested capacity.

Does nothing if the requested capacity is not larger than the current capacity, avoiding unnecessary work and maintaining existing memory layout.

Example:

# Requesting 100 entities will allocate capacity for 128 (next power of 2)
archetype.reserve(100)  # Actually reserves 128

# Requesting 64 entities allocates exactly 64 (already power of 2)
archetype.reserve(64)   # Actually reserves 64

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • new_capacity (Int): The minimum required capacity. The actual allocated capacity will be next_power_of_two(new_capacity) to maintain power-of-2 growth.

init_component_range

Initializes the component with the given Type T for multiple consecutive, uninitialized entities starting with the given index.

def init_component_range[T: ComponentType](mut self, start_entity_idx: Int, count: Int, value: T)

Unlike Archetype.set_component_range, this does not destroy any prior value at the target rows: it places a fresh copy of value directly into each row. Use this for rows that were just appended (e.g. via Archetype.extend) or migrated (e.g. via Archetype.unsafe_move_all_from_archetype) and therefore hold uninitialized memory for T.

def unsafe_move_all_from_archetype[source_origin: MutOrigin](mut self, source: Pointer[Self, source_origin], excluded_components: _BitMask[Int(256)] = _BitMask()) -> Int

item.title: ArchetypeRowAccessor
item.description:
Development reference · Larecs 1.0.0b1 · revision 8d289cca4516. Host threading and device execution are experimental. Compatibility and status.

Mojo structSource

ArchetypeRowAccessor

@memory_only
struct ArchetypeRowAccessor[archetype_mutability: Bool, //, archetype_origin: Origin[mut=archetype_mutability], *ComponentTypes: ComponentType, *, filter: Filter[filter._include, filter._exclude, filter._is_exclusive, filter._read, filter._written] = Filter()]

Accessor for an Entity.

Caution: use this only in the context it was created in. In particular, do not store it anywhere.

Aliases

Archetype

The archetype of the entity.

Archetype = Archetype[ComponentTypes]

Parameters

  • archetype_mutability (Bool): Whether the reference to the list is mutable.
  • archetype_origin (Origin[mut=archetype_mutability]): The lifetime of the List.
  • *ComponentTypes (ComponentType): The types of the components.
  • filter (Filter[filter._include, filter._exclude, filter._is_exclusive, filter._read, filter._written]): The compile-time Filter this accessor was created with, if any. When a component is included by filter, get[T]() accesses it with a compile-time guarantee that it exists, instead of unsafe_get[T]()’s runtime check. Accessors created without a filter (the default) can only use unsafe_get/has.

Implemented traits

AnyType, Deinitable, Movable

Methods

Expand all   Collapse all

get_entity

Returns the entity of the accessor.

def get_entity(self) -> Entity

Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

Entity: The entity of the accessor.

get

Returns a reference to a component guaranteed by this accessor’s filter.

def get[T: ComponentType](ref self) -> ref[archetype_origin] T

Parameters:

  • T (ComponentType): The type of the component.

Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

ref[archetype_origin] T: A reference to the component of the entity.

Raises:

LarecsError: Never in practice – T’s presence is guaranteed by filter (see Constraints below). Declared because the underlying storage lookup is, in general, a runtime check.

Constraints:

T must be included by the Filter this accessor was created with (e.g. via HostStorage.query’s Filter.include). Every archetype an accessor with that filter can be created for is guaranteed to carry T, so this is enforced at compile time rather than by a runtime check. Use unsafe_get[T]() for components the filter doesn’t guarantee, or has[T]() to check first.

unsafe_get

Returns a reference to the given component, checked at runtime.

def unsafe_get[T: ComponentType](ref self) -> ref[archetype_origin] T

Unlike get[T](), T need not be included by this accessor’s filter – this is the escape hatch for components that may or may not be present on the underlying archetype. Check with has[T]() first, or catch the raised error.

Parameters:

  • T (ComponentType): The type of the component.

Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

ref[archetype_origin] T: A reference to the component of the entity.

Raises:

LarecsError: If the entity’s archetype does not contain the component.
